2e9984c2e084.Azure Blob Storage: Blob Storage holds unstructured objects but is not an OCI registry, so Docker and Kubernetes cannot push or pull versioned images from it.
2e9984c2e084.Azure Container Apps: Container Apps runs containers pulled from a registry. It does not store or version the images itself.
2e9984c2e084.Azure Artifacts feeds: Azure Artifacts in Azure DevOps hosts packages such as NuGet, npm and Maven. It does not host container images, which belong in a container registry.

26f892bf9a14.Azure Container Instances: Container Instances runs existing images on demand. It does not build images from source or trigger on code commits.
26f892bf9a14.Azure Container Apps jobs: Container Apps jobs run finite tasks from images that already exist. Building and pushing images on commit is the job of ACR Tasks.
26f892bf9a14.Azure Container Registry webhooks: Registry webhooks send notifications when images are pushed or deleted. They do not build images from source code.

fb7c28e71652.az acr import --name myreg --source app:: az acr import copies an existing image from another registry. It does not build from a local Dockerfile.
fb7c28e71652.az acr run --registry myreg --cmd app:v1: az acr run runs a command or multi-step task in a container. With --cmd it runs an image rather than building and pushing one from the Dockerfile.
fb7c28e71652.az acr task create --registry myreg --im: az acr task create defines a task that runs on triggers later, and it also needs a context and --name. It does not build and push the current folder immediately.

f2578221aa93.Pass it as a Docker build argument in th: Build arguments are captured at build time and can end up in image layers or history, which is baking the value into the image.
f2578221aa93.Mount it from an Azure Files share liste: Storing a secret in a file share and referencing it in the Dockerfile still couples it to the image and lacks secret management. App settings are the supported way.
f2578221aa93.Store it as an ENV instruction set in th: An ENV instruction writes the value into the image configuration, which is exactly what the question wants to avoid.

7896b994653c.Azure Container Instances: Container Instances runs single container groups without revisions, built-in traffic splitting or scale-to-zero autoscaling.
7896b994653c.Azure Kubernetes Service: AKS gives revisions and ingress only through Kubernetes objects you manage yourself, so you still operate a Kubernetes cluster.
7896b994653c.Azure App Service for Containers: App Service runs containers on a plan that does not scale to zero and has no revision model like Container Apps.

cfd7c2ce371c.Single revision mode with a new revision: In single revision mode the new revision replaces the old one, so you cannot split traffic by percentage.
cfd7c2ce371c.Two deployment slots with a 10% routing: Deployment slots and traffic routing are App Service features. Container Apps uses revisions, not slots.
cfd7c2ce371c.Multiple replicas with a 10% scale rule: Scale rules control replica count, not how ingress traffic is split between versions.

1b1a42223848.A KEDA scale rule for Azure Event Hubs: The Event Hubs scaler measures consumer lag on an event hub, not the length of a Service Bus queue.
1b1a42223848.An HTTP scale rule on concurrent request: HTTP scale rules react to incoming HTTP requests. A queue consumer gets no HTTP traffic to scale on.
1b1a42223848.A custom CPU scale rule set to 70%: CPU-based rules react to load inside replicas and cannot scale out from zero based on waiting messages.

b64032f3c1d1.The container app's ingress settings: Ingress settings control how traffic reaches one app. The virtual network and Log Analytics destination are set on the environment.
b64032f3c1d1.Each container app revision template: Revision templates define containers, scale and volumes for one app. They cannot set the shared network or logging workspace.
b64032f3c1d1.The Azure Monitor diagnostic settings: Diagnostic settings can route logs, but the shared virtual network and logs destination for the apps are defined on the environment.

558da9cef965.kubectl create -f service.yaml --dry-run: With --dry-run nothing is created on the cluster, so the app is not deployed.
558da9cef965.az aks command invoke deployment.yaml: az aks command invoke runs a command through the cluster with --command. Passing a file name alone does not apply a manifest.
558da9cef965.kubectl rollout status -f deployment.yam: kubectl rollout status watches the progress of an existing rollout. It does not create or update resources.

305a9a3a15cf.DaemonSet: A DaemonSet runs one pod per node rather than a chosen number of identical replicas.
305a9a3a15cf.StatefulSet: A StatefulSet manages pods with stable identities and ordered updates, used for stateful workloads rather than identical stateless pods.
305a9a3a15cf.Job: A Job runs pods until they complete successfully. It does not keep a desired pod count running or do rolling updates.

48fafd3832b6.Enable the registry admin user and set i: The admin user is meant for testing, and using it in pods still requires an image pull secret, which the question rules out.
48fafd3832b6.Assign the AcrPush role to the cluster's: Pulls are done by the kubelet identity, not the control plane identity, and AcrPush is broader than needed.
48fafd3832b6.Create a repository-scoped registry toke: Repository-scoped tokens are passed as credentials in an image pull secret, which the question wants to avoid.

5ad9f69b4a7c.kubectl get pod <pod> -o yaml: This shows the pod object and status, such as restart count, but not the container's console output.
5ad9f69b4a7c.kubectl top pod <pod> --containers: kubectl top shows CPU and memory usage from the metrics server, not container logs.
5ad9f69b4a7c.kubectl get events --watch: Events show scheduling and restart reasons but not what the application wrote to stdout before crashing.

394396de27fe.Container Apps revision history and the: AppServiceConsoleLogs and AppServicePlatformLogs are App Service tables. Container Apps writes to ContainerAppConsoleLogs and ContainerAppSystemLogs.
394396de27fe.Container Apps metrics explorer and the: ContainerLogV2 and KubeEvents come from Container insights on AKS. Container Apps uses its own ContainerApp log tables.
394396de27fe.Container Apps ingress logs and the Azur: The activity log records control plane operations, not console output, and Container Apps logs go to their own ContainerApp tables.

9577b27c71ef.kubectl get pod <pod>: kubectl get shows a one-line status such as ErrImagePull, but not the list of recent events with details.
9577b27c71ef.kubectl logs <pod>: kubectl logs shows container output. If the image never pulled there is no container output to show.
9577b27c71ef.kubectl top pod <pod>: kubectl top shows resource usage from the metrics server, not events.

0f36476e978e.Consistent prefix: Consistent prefix guarantees reads never see out-of-order writes, so it has an ordering guarantee.
0f36476e978e.Session: Session guarantees read-your-own-writes and ordering within a session, at slightly higher cost than eventual.
0f36476e978e.Bounded staleness: Bounded staleness guarantees order and a maximum lag, which costs more latency than eventual.

ed2710ce0e2b.Strong: Strong gives linearizable reads but is not the default and has higher latency.
ed2710ce0e2b.Consistent prefix: Consistent prefix guarantees ordering but not read-your-own-writes, and it is not the default.
ed2710ce0e2b.Bounded staleness: Bounded staleness limits lag by time or versions. It is not the default level.

65ce3f12a055.Add composite indexes for every property: Extra indexes add index maintenance work to each write, so write RU cost goes up, not down.
65ce3f12a055.Switch the indexing mode from consistent: Lazy indexing mode is deprecated for new containers and does not reduce the RU charge of writes.
65ce3f12a055.Lower the default consistency level to e: Consistency level affects read cost and latency. Write RU cost is driven mainly by item size and indexing.

70130ee0db55.A composite index on the embedding path: Composite indexes serve multi-property ORDER BY queries and full-text policies serve keyword search. Neither enables vector similarity search.
70130ee0db55.A spatial index on the embedding path an: Spatial indexes support GeoJSON queries such as ST_DISTANCE. They do not index embedding vectors.
70130ee0db55.A unique key policy and a range index on: Range indexes and unique keys work on scalar values. Vector search needs a vector embedding policy and vector index.

a838f9df857a.ST_DISTANCE: ST_DISTANCE returns the distance between two GeoJSON points, not between embedding vectors.
a838f9df857a.FullTextScore: FullTextScore ranks items by BM25 keyword relevance, not vector similarity.
a838f9df857a.RRF: RRF combines rankings from multiple scoring functions in hybrid search. It does not compute vector similarity itself.

9e593e496772.A Cosmos DB post-trigger defined on the: Server-side triggers must be named explicitly on each request and cannot call an external embedding model.
9e593e496772.An Event Grid system topic for the Cosmo: Cosmos DB Event Grid events cover control plane operations, not item inserts and updates. Item changes come from the change feed.
9e593e496772.Azure Synapse Link with the analytical s: Synapse Link replicates data for analytics. It does not trigger code for each inserted or updated item.

0c0237f7dc7a.A property used in every query filter, w: A frequently filtered property helps avoid cross-partition queries, but with few distinct values it still creates hot, oversized partitions. Cardinality and even spread come first.
0c0237f7dc7a.Low cardinality so related items always: Few distinct values creates large, hot logical partitions and can hit the 20 GB logical partition limit.
0c0237f7dc7a.A property that is updated often so data: The partition key value of an item cannot be changed in place, and frequent changes do not help distribution.

0ff44a38dcd2.azure_ai: The azure_ai extension calls Azure OpenAI and AI services from SQL, but the vector data type comes from pgvector.
0ff44a38dcd2.pg_diskann: pg_diskann adds a DiskANN index method and depends on the vector extension, which supplies the vector data type.
0ff44a38dcd2.postgis: PostGIS adds geospatial types and functions, not embedding vectors.

dca26f5253c5.<#>: In pgvector <#> is negative inner product.

c75094e6c527.A GIN index on the embedding column for: GIN indexes serve arrays, JSONB and full text. They do not support pgvector distance operators.
c75094e6c527.A B-tree index on the embedding column p: B-tree indexes support equality and range comparisons, not nearest neighbor ordering by distance, and ANALYZE only refreshes statistics.
c75094e6c527.A BRIN index on the embedding column for: BRIN indexes summarize block ranges for ordered data and cannot speed up vector similarity search.

e860f5a5b546.Order the whole table by embedding dista: Filtering after LIMIT can drop all rows for the tenant and leaks other tenants' rows to the app.
e860f5a5b546.Combine a GROUP BY on tenant_id with MIN: GROUP BY with MIN returns one aggregate value per tenant rather than the nearest documents.
e860f5a5b546.Use a full text tsvector search on tenan: Full text search ranks keyword matches. It does not measure semantic similarity between embeddings.

9dc9f89388e0.Read replicas, for example with in-regio: Read replicas spread read load but each still has its own connection limit, so a connection per request still exhausts it.
9dc9f89388e0.A higher max_connections, for example se: max_connections is capped by the compute size and each connection uses memory. It does not fix opening a connection per request.
9dc9f89388e0.Elastic clusters, for example with Citus: Distributing data across nodes does not stop the app from opening a new connection for each request.

3f5301b7f4a5.work_mem: work_mem is used by sort and hash operations in queries. Index builds use maintenance_work_mem.
3f5301b7f4a5.shared_buffers: shared_buffers sets the server-wide page cache and needs a restart. It is not the per-session index build memory.
3f5301b7f4a5.effective_cache_size: effective_cache_size is only a planner estimate and does not allocate memory for index builds.

105ac9d4be7c.Azure Cosmos DB analytical store: The analytical store is a columnar copy for analytics, not a low-latency cache for prompt responses.
105ac9d4be7c.Azure Front Door caching rules: Front Door caches HTTP responses by URL, typically GET requests. LLM prompts are POST bodies, so it cannot cache answers per prompt.
105ac9d4be7c.Azure API Management rate limits: Rate limits throttle callers. They do not return a stored answer for a repeated prompt.

cea4e1aeda96.A maxmemory eviction policy: Eviction removes keys only under memory pressure, not after a fixed 10 minutes.
cea4e1aeda96.A data persistence RDB snapshot: Persistence saves data to disk. It does not remove keys after a time.
cea4e1aeda96.Keyspace notifications on keys: Keyspace notifications publish events when keys change or expire. They do not set the expiry.

36205363e54e.Switch the cache to the allkeys-lru evic: Eviction removes keys only when memory is full, so the stale copy can still be served.
36205363e54e.Enable active geo-replication for the ca: Geo-replication copies data between caches. It does not detect database changes.
36205363e54e.Increase the cache key's expiration time: A longer TTL keeps the stale value longer. The key should be removed when the record changes.

e1e74cc0c9e4.JSON documents with the RedisJSON module: RedisJSON stores and updates JSON documents. Vector indexing and similarity queries come from RediSearch.
e1e74cc0c9e4.Probabilistic filters with RedisBloom: RedisBloom offers Bloom filters and sketches for membership tests, not vector similarity search.
e1e74cc0c9e4.Time series data with RedisTimeSeries: RedisTimeSeries stores and aggregates time-stamped samples. It does not run vector similarity search.

0e31ad3b3d78.Azure Event Hubs: Event Hubs is a partitioned event stream for high-throughput telemetry, without per-message locks or dead-lettering of individual jobs.
0e31ad3b3d78.Azure Event Grid: Event Grid pushes notifications about events. It is not a work queue with message locks for competing workers.
0e31ad3b3d78.Azure Queue Storage: Queue Storage lacks built-in dead-lettering, duplicate detection and sessions, so it is not the reliable choice the scenario describes.

67901eadb343.A queue with one session per service: Sessions group related messages in a queue, but each message is still received by only one consumer.
67901eadb343.A partitioned queue with duplicate detec: A queue delivers each message to one consumer. Partitioning and duplicate detection do not create copies.
67901eadb343.Auto-forwarding from one queue to anothe: Auto-forwarding moves a message to one destination. It does not give every service its own copy.

3dd917cf37f2.It is moved to the transfer dead-letter: The transfer dead-letter queue holds messages that failed during auto-forwarding or transfer, not ones exceeding MaxDeliveryCount.
3dd917cf37f2.It is deferred until the consumer reques: Deferral happens only when the receiver explicitly defers a message. It is not the automatic result of exceeding the delivery count.
3dd917cf37f2.It is abandoned and its lock is renewed: Abandoning releases the lock for another attempt. After MaxDeliveryCount the message is dead-lettered instead.

7770bd7452fd.ReceiveAndDelete, then abandon on failur: ReceiveAndDelete removes the message as soon as it is received, so there is nothing to abandon if processing fails.
7770bd7452fd.PeekLock, then defer the message: Deferring sets the message aside for later retrieval by sequence number. It does not remove it after success.
7770bd7452fd.Peek, then complete the message: Peek reads a message without locking it, so it cannot be completed.

3ca81114e9d0.Azure Event Hubs: Event Hubs is a pull-based stream that consumers read from. It is not the service that pushes Blob Storage events to handlers.
3ca81114e9d0.Azure Logic Apps: A Logic Apps workflow consumes events. The Blob Storage BlobCreated event itself is delivered by Event Grid.
3ca81114e9d0.Azure Storage queues: Storage queues need consumers to poll for messages, which is not push-based delivery.

0979fffbace7.An event subscription filter on subject: Subject begins with matches the start of the subject, which is the container path, not the file extension.
0979fffbace7.A topic input schema mapping on the data: Input schema mapping applies to custom topics and maps fields. It does not filter Blob Storage events.
0979fffbace7.A dead-letter destination for events not: Dead-lettering stores events that could not be delivered. It does not filter which events are sent.

d1305a8cab7e.Retries every 5 minutes for up to 7 days: Event Grid defaults are up to 30 attempts within 24 hours, and dead-lettering goes to a storage container you configure, not a topic queue.
d1305a8cab7e.Holds the event in the topic until the h: Event Grid has a maximum time to live of 24 hours by default. It does not keep events indefinitely.
d1305a8cab7e.Dead-letters it immediately to the subsc: Dead-lettering is off by default and only happens after retries are exhausted or for certain errors.

973ba65a8b4d.A system topic for your app: System topics carry events from Azure services, not events your own application publishes.
973ba65a8b4d.A partner topic (or partner namespace): Partner topics receive events from third-party SaaS partners, not from your own application.
973ba65a8b4d.An Event Hubs namespace with a consumer: Event Hubs is a streaming service, not an Event Grid topic with filtered event subscriptions.

2fd6bf4636f7.Azure Functions with a Timer trigger: A timer trigger runs on a schedule and does not expose an HTTP API.
2fd6bf4636f7.Azure Logic Apps Standard on a dedicated: Logic Apps Standard runs on a Workflow Standard plan you size, which is not the lightweight serverless API option.
2fd6bf4636f7.Azure App Service on a Basic plan: A Basic App Service plan has fixed instances that you manage and pay for, and it does not autoscale.

6f3bc160dce0.An input binding: Input bindings read data into a function. Writing to a queue needs an output binding.
6f3bc160dce0.A Service Bus trigger: A trigger starts the function when a message arrives. It does not send messages.
6f3bc160dce0.A host.json extension: host.json configures extension behavior such as retries, but the write itself is declared with an output binding.

3849fd0cd6e9.One or more: A function cannot have several triggers. Use multiple functions instead.
3849fd0cd6e9.Zero or one: A function must have a trigger to be invoked, so zero is not valid.
3849fd0cd6e9.Up to two: There is no limit of two. Each function has exactly one trigger.

4c13aa03dc8e.Elastic Premium plan: Elastic Premium keeps at least one instance always running and bills per instance, so it does not scale to zero.
4c13aa03dc8e.Consumption plan on Linux: The legacy Linux Consumption plan does not support virtual network integration and is being retired.
4c13aa03dc8e.Dedicated App Service plan: Dedicated plans bill for allocated instances and do not scale to zero.

ace8492203cb.function.json: function.json holds the trigger and bindings for a single function, not app-wide settings.
ace8492203cb.local.settings.json: local.settings.json holds app settings for local development only and is not deployed to Azure.
ace8492203cb.extensions.csproj: extensions.csproj lists binding extension packages to install, not logging or extension behavior settings.

1462ab7fa822.From the function.json binding file as l: Bindings reference the name of an app setting. Putting literal connection strings in function.json is not how production config is read.
1462ab7fa822.From host.json, which is deployed with t: host.json holds runtime and extension configuration, not connection strings, which come from app settings.
1462ab7fa822.From local.settings.json, which is publi: local.settings.json is for local development and is not published to Azure by Core Tools.

6ce833c7bb02.Azure App Configuration: App Configuration is for non-secret settings and feature flags. Secrets should be in Key Vault, optionally referenced from App Configuration.
6ce833c7bb02.Azure Managed HSM: Managed HSM stores cryptographic keys only. It does not store secrets such as API keys.
6ce833c7bb02.Azure Storage Table: Table storage is not a secret store and lacks per-secret access control, versioning and rotation.

f6d0932e3ec3.A service principal with a client secret: A client secret is a stored credential, and Key Vault Reader grants management plane access only, not secret values.
f6d0932e3ec3.A managed identity with an RBAC role suc: Key Vault Certificate User lets an identity read certificate contents, not general secrets.
f6d0932e3ec3.A managed identity with the Key Vault Cr: That role allows wrap and unwrap operations with keys. It does not grant reading secrets.

cc5721005945.Key Vault soft delete, and have apps rea: Soft delete protects deleted secrets for recovery. It does not rotate secrets.
cc5721005945.Key Vault expiration dates, and have app: An expiration date does not create a new value, and pinning a version means apps never pick up the rotated secret.
cc5721005945.Key Vault backup and restore, and have a: Backup and restore copy a secret for recovery. They do not rotate it and redeploying adds app impact.

12e69d5d50fa.Azure Key Vault: Key Vault is for secrets, keys and certificates. It has no feature flag management.
12e69d5d50fa.Azure API Management: API Management has named values for policies but is not a central configuration and feature flag store for apps.
12e69d5d50fa.Azure Resource Manager tags: Tags label resources for organization and billing. Apps do not read feature flags from them.

c1a2500e02e1.Use snapshots: Snapshots capture a point-in-time set of key-values. They are not how one key holds per-environment values.
c1a2500e02e1.Use tags on key-values: Tags add metadata for filtering, but key plus label is what makes separate values of the same key.
c1a2500e02e1.Use feature filters: Feature filters control when a feature flag is on, not separate values of a regular key.

b522eb8336b0.A feature flag with a filter: A feature flag turns features on or off. It does not point to a Key Vault secret.
b522eb8336b0.A plain key-value with the URI: A plain key-value is not resolved by the client library, so the app would just get the URI string.
b522eb8336b0.A snapshot of the store: A snapshot is a point-in-time set of key-values. It does not reference a secret in Key Vault.

f04e2ac00b8b.OpenAPI: OpenAPI describes REST API contracts. It does not emit traces.
f04e2ac00b8b.OpenMetrics: OpenMetrics is a format for exposing metrics, not for distributed traces across services.
f04e2ac00b8b.Fluent Bit: Fluent Bit is a log processor and forwarder, not the open standard for instrumenting distributed traces.

8f235525c872.A shared span ID reused by every service: Each span has its own span ID. The trace ID is what is shared across services.
8f235525c872.A shared session ID stored in the Applic: Cloud role name identifies a service in the application map, and session ID groups user sessions, not spans of a request.
8f235525c872.A shared operation name set on each depe: Operation name is a readable label shared by many requests. It does not link the spans of one request.

42a557c284a8.requests | where timestamp > ago(1h) and: resultCode holds the HTTP status code, not a boolean, so this does not find failures.
42a557c284a8.requests | filter timestamp > ago(1h) an: KQL has no filter operator for this. Rows are filtered with where.
42a557c284a8.requests | where timestamp < ago(1h) and: timestamp < ago(1h) returns requests older than one hour, not the last hour.

b4da3d598fc6.extend count() by operation_Name: extend adds calculated columns to each row. It cannot aggregate or group.
b4da3d598fc6.project count() by operation_Name: project selects and computes columns per row and does not group rows.
b4da3d598fc6.make-series count() on operation_Name: make-series builds time series arrays and needs on a numeric or datetime axis column with by for grouping, so this syntax is wrong.

e5281ccc8ec8.summarize avg(duration) by timestamp, 5m: This groups by each distinct timestamp and treats 5m as another expression, so it does not create 5-minute buckets.
e5281ccc8ec8.make-series avg(duration) by bin(5m, tim: make-series uses on timestamp with a step, and bin takes the value first then the size, so this is invalid.
e5281ccc8ec8.extend avg(duration) by bin(timestamp, 5: extend adds per-row columns and cannot aggregate with by.

9877f933231a.Container insights: Container insights collects container and node metrics and logs, not request and dependency telemetry from your code.
9877f933231a.VM insights: VM insights monitors virtual machine performance and dependencies between processes, not application requests and exceptions.
9877f933231a.Network Watcher: Network Watcher diagnoses network connectivity. It does not collect application telemetry.

40d7cde37372.The Live Metrics view in Application Ins: Live Metrics shows near real-time aggregate rates. It does not break one request into its dependency spans.
40d7cde37372.The Usage Funnels view in Application In: Funnels analyze how users move through steps in the app, not dependency durations.
40d7cde37372.The Availability tests view in Applicati: Availability tests ping endpoints from outside. They do not show which downstream call slowed a request.

b5142a568e7c.An Azure Monitor activity log alert on a: Activity log alerts fire on control plane operations and health events, not on application exception rates.
b5142a568e7c.An Application Insights availability tes: Availability tests check whether an endpoint responds. They do not measure the exception rate of the API.
b5142a568e7c.An Azure Monitor diagnostic setting on a: Diagnostic settings export telemetry to destinations. They do not evaluate thresholds or notify anyone.

30a7f41ba200.ManagedIdentityCredential: ManagedIdentityCredential works only where a managed identity exists, so it fails on a developer machine.
30a7f41ba200.AzureCliCredential: AzureCliCredential needs a signed-in Azure CLI and normally is not available in the hosted Azure environment.
30a7f41ba200.ClientSecretCredential: ClientSecretCredential requires a stored client secret and does not adapt to the environment.

e5b1f0d9658c.HTTP scaling with 1 to 10 replicas: The default HTTP rule has a minimum of 0 replicas, not 1, so the app can scale to zero when idle.
e5b1f0d9658c.CPU scaling with 0 to 10 replicas: Container Apps does not add a CPU rule by default. With ingress enabled and no rule, it applies an HTTP rule.
e5b1f0d9658c.HTTP scaling with 0 to 30 replicas: The default HTTP rule caps the app at 10 replicas, not 30. You must set maxReplicas yourself to go higher.

b26577e08753.It gets a default HTTP rule and scales f: The default HTTP rule only applies when ingress is enabled. With ingress disabled there is no HTTP traffic to scale on.
b26577e08753.It keeps one replica because minReplicas: minReplicas defaults to 0, so no replica is kept. The app scales to zero and nothing wakes it up.
b26577e08753.It fails deployment until a scale rule i: This configuration deploys without error. The problem appears at runtime, when the app scales to zero with no trigger to restart it.

a5e22afc82c5.A secretRef pointing to a secret that ho: A secretRef supplies a connection string, which is exactly what the requirement rules out. Managed identity auth uses the identity property on the rule.
a5e22afc82c5.A Dapr pub/sub component that authentica: A Dapr component handles messaging inside the app, not the scaler's authentication. The scale rule itself needs the identity property.
a5e22afc82c5.A KEDA TriggerAuthentication resource wi: TriggerAuthentication is a KEDA object you create in AKS. Container Apps does not expose it, and you set identity directly on the scale rule instead.

cd9ab9a4a214.KEDA polls custom rules every 300 second: Custom scale rules are polled every 30 seconds. The 300 seconds is the cooldown applied when removing the last replica.
cd9ab9a4a214.Scale-down waits for a 10-minute stabili: There is no 10-minute window on every removal. The 300-second cooldown applies only when scaling from the final replica to zero.
cd9ab9a4a214.minReplicas defaults to 1, so the last r: minReplicas defaults to 0, and the app does reach zero on its own. The delay comes from the 300-second cooldown, not a restart.

4dd142f32496.A scheduled Container Apps job: Scheduled jobs run on a cron schedule, not once per queue message. Event-driven jobs start an execution for each event.
4dd142f32496.A manual Container Apps job: Manual jobs start only when you trigger them through the API or CLI. They do not react to queue messages by themselves.
4dd142f32496.A container app with a Service Bus scale: Container apps run continuously and restart containers that exit. Tasks that run to completion and exit fit Container Apps jobs.

4faf0fbf6501.A Container Apps secret holding the pass: A copied value is static and does not change when the Key Vault secret rotates. A Key Vault reference through managed identity picks up new values.
4faf0fbf6501.An environment variable with a Key Vault: The @Microsoft.KeyVault reference syntax is for App Service and Functions app settings. Container Apps uses secrets that reference Key Vault instead.
4faf0fbf6501.A Key Vault CSI driver volume mounted in: The Secrets Store CSI driver is an AKS add-on and is not available in Container Apps. Container Apps secrets reference Key Vault directly.

8ac5fb3ab67b.The SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT setti: This setting controls build automation for code deployments. It does not tell App Service which port a custom container listens on.
8ac5fb3ab67b.The Always On general setting to On: Always On keeps the app loaded between requests. It does not change the port App Service sends traffic to.
8ac5fb3ab67b.The HTTP version general setting to 2.0: The HTTP version setting changes the protocol for clients, not the container port. WEBSITES_PORT sets the port for custom containers.

dcfc52b533f5.An ACR task with a timer trigger set to: A timer trigger rebuilds on a schedule whether or not the base changed. The base image update trigger rebuilds when the base image is updated.
dcfc52b533f5.An ACR webhook that fires on the base im: Webhooks only send a notification to an endpoint. They do not rebuild images and do not track base image dependencies.
dcfc52b533f5.An ACR task with a source code commit tr: A commit trigger fires when the Git repository changes, not when the base image receives patches.

76b97c5816f4.Geo-replication, which requires the Stan: Geo-replication is a Premium tier feature. Standard registries cannot add replicas in other regions.
76b97c5816f4.Zone redundancy, which requires the Prem: Zone redundancy spreads a registry across availability zones within one region. It does not bring images closer to teams in other regions.
76b97c5816f4.Artifact cache, which works in the Basic: Artifact cache pulls upstream images into the same registry. It does not create regional replicas, so remote pulls stay slow.

8f771c6d4e10.The Secrets Store CSI driver with a serv: This stores a client secret in the cluster, which the requirement rules out. Workload ID issues tokens through federation with no stored secret.
8f771c6d4e10.Microsoft Entra pod-managed identity wit: Pod-managed identity is deprecated and has been replaced by Microsoft Entra Workload ID for new workloads.
8f771c6d4e10.A Kubernetes service account token mount: Key Vault does not accept Kubernetes tokens. The token must be exchanged for an Entra token through a federated credential.

c788a2abf5f3.A liveness probe that fails until the mo: A failing liveness probe makes the kubelet restart the container, so the model may never finish loading. Readiness controls traffic.
c788a2abf5f3.A preStop lifecycle hook that waits for: preStop hooks run when a container is being terminated, not at startup. They do not keep traffic away from a loading pod.
c788a2abf5f3.A PodDisruptionBudget with minAvailable: A PodDisruptionBudget limits voluntary evictions. It does not stop a Service from sending traffic to pods that are not ready.

339dea800216.The containers have no CPU resource limi: HPA computes CPU utilization against requests, not limits. Missing limits alone do not cause unknown metrics.
339dea800216.The cluster autoscaler is disabled on th: The cluster autoscaler adds nodes. It does not provide the CPU metrics that HPA reads, so it does not cause unknown values.
339dea800216.The deployment has no PodDisruptionBudge: A PodDisruptionBudget controls voluntary evictions and has no effect on HPA metric calculation.

0a368e9476ac.diskANN, because it supports at most 512: diskANN supports up to 4,096 dimensions, so 1,536-dimension vectors can use it.
0a368e9476ac.quantizedFlat, because it supports at mo: quantizedFlat supports up to 4,096 dimensions, so it works for 1,536 dimensions.
0a368e9476ac.None, since all three types support up t: Only quantizedFlat and diskANN reach 4,096 dimensions. flat is limited to 505, so it cannot be used here.

48b92c836ffd.flat: flat is limited to 505 dimensions and is not the recommended choice for filtered search scopes. quantizedFlat fits scopes up to about 50,000 vectors.
48b92c836ffd.diskANN: diskANN is recommended for larger search scopes, above roughly 50,000 vectors. For about 5,000 vectors per tenant, quantizedFlat is recommended.
48b92c836ffd.hnsw: HNSW is not a vector index type in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL. The supported types are flat, quantizedFlat and diskANN.

221a2a101fa6.Update the distanceFunction in the vecto: Settings of an existing vector embedding policy cannot be edited in place. You must remove the path's configuration and add it back.
221a2a101fa6.Change the vector index type to flat fir: Switching index types does not unlock in-place edits. The vector policy for the path must be dropped and re-added.
221a2a101fa6.Disable vector search on the container,: Vector search cannot be disabled on a container once it is enabled. You drop and re-add the path's policy and index instead.

ff565f832fb9.Without TOP N the query falls back to th: The index type does not change based on the query. The cost comes from returning far more results than needed.
ff565f832fb9.Without TOP N the query runs cross-parti: Whether a query is cross-partition depends on the partition key filter, not on TOP. The extra RUs come from returning too many results.
ff565f832fb9.Without TOP N VectorDistance computes sc: bruteForce defaults to false and is not changed by omitting TOP. The query costs more because it returns many more results.

772dc893c886.diskANN needs at least 10,000 vectors, o: The threshold is 1,000 vectors, and below it the service runs a full scan rather than using a flat index.
772dc893c886.diskANN does not support cosine, so the: diskANN supports cosine, dot product and Euclidean distance. The full scan happens because fewer than 1,000 vectors are indexed.
772dc893c886.diskANN requires float16 vectors, otherw: diskANN works with float32 vectors as well. The higher RU cost comes from having fewer than 1,000 indexed vectors.

6f4a6a46f496.Use float32 as the vector data type: float32 is the full-size default, so it does not reduce storage. float16 halves it.
6f4a6a46f496.Use euclidean as the distance function: The distance function changes how similarity is scored, not how many bytes each vector uses.
6f4a6a46f496.Use flat as the vector index type: flat stores full vectors for exact search and does not reduce vector storage. Changing the data type to float16 does.

f5870542bb3a.Latest version mode, which needs continu: Latest version mode does not capture deletes, and it does not need continuous backup.
f5870542bb3a.All versions and deletes mode, which nee: All versions and deletes mode requires continuous backup, not periodic backup.
f5870542bb3a.Latest version mode with the change feed: Latest version mode does not emit deletes or TTL expirations, whatever consumer reads it.

9c4158eb10c9.Yes, ordering is guaranteed only within: Order is guaranteed per logical partition key value. Items with different keys in the same physical partition have no guaranteed order.
9c4158eb10c9.No, the change feed is ordered globally: The change feed has no global order across partition keys, so out-of-order changes for different products are expected.
9c4158eb10c9.Yes, but only when the pull model is use: Ordering rules are the same for the pull model and the change feed processor. Order is guaranteed only within a partition key.

59268963e39b.An Azure Storage checkpoint container: Blob storage checkpoints are used by the Event Hubs processor. The Cosmos DB change feed processor stores leases in a Cosmos DB container.
59268963e39b.An Event Hubs consumer group: Consumer groups belong to Event Hubs. The change feed processor distributes work through a lease container.
59268963e39b.A Durable Functions task hub: A task hub stores Durable Functions orchestration state. The change feed processor needs a lease container instead.

5e78a2c325ba.A unique key policy on the tenantId and: A unique key policy enforces uniqueness within a logical partition. It does not lift the 20 GB logical partition limit.
5e78a2c325ba.A composite index on the tenantId and us: Composite indexes speed up queries with multiple filters or sorts. They do not change how data is partitioned.
5e78a2c325ba.Partition merge to combine tenants into: Partition merge reduces the number of physical partitions. A logical partition key value is still limited to 20 GB.

53b209ec5207.A query filtered by id and partition key: A query goes through the query engine and costs more than a point read, even when it is scoped to one partition.
53b209ec5207.A change feed read filtered to that part: The change feed returns changes over time, not a direct lookup of one item, and costs more than a point read.
53b209ec5207.A cross-partition query using the id ind: A cross-partition query fans out to many partitions and is far more expensive than a point read.

672c67e96098.Autoscale throughput, which scales betwe: Autoscale scales down to 10% of the configured maximum, not 50%.
672c67e96098.Serverless throughput, which scales betw: Serverless accounts have no provisioned floor or maximum to configure. The 10% to 100% range belongs to autoscale.
672c67e96098.Manual throughput with a burst capacity: Manual throughput stays fixed. Burst capacity only uses idle accumulated capacity for short spikes, it does not scale between a floor and a maximum.

d91601dca9e1.IVFFlat supports only L2 distance, so co: IVFFlat supports L2, inner product and cosine distance. The poor recall comes from building lists on an empty table.
d91601dca9e1.IVFFlat needs hnsw.ef_search raised afte: hnsw.ef_search applies to HNSW indexes only. IVFFlat recall depends on its lists, which must be built from loaded data.
d91601dca9e1.IVFFlat rebalances its lists on insert,: IVFFlat does not rebalance lists on insert, and VACUUM does not rebuild them. You rebuild the index after loading data.

a49dbc06bc66.Increase ef_construction: ef_construction is set when the HNSW index is built, not at query time.
a49dbc06bc66.Increase ivfflat.probes: ivfflat.probes affects IVFFlat indexes only. It has no effect on HNSW searches.
a49dbc06bc66.Decrease hnsw.ef_search: A smaller candidate list lowers recall. You increase hnsw.ef_search to improve it.

c9c1f8cabc0a.hnsw.ef_search: hnsw.ef_search controls the HNSW candidate list size and has no effect on IVFFlat lists.
c9c1f8cabc0a.lists: lists is an index build option that sets how many lists exist, not how many are scanned per query.
c9c1f8cabc0a.ivfflat.iterative_scan: iterative_scan controls whether filtered queries keep scanning to return enough rows. ivfflat.probes sets the number of lists scanned.

e250de0ff1e9.pg_diskann: pg_diskann adds the DiskANN vector index. It does not call Azure OpenAI to generate embeddings.
e250de0ff1e9.vector: The vector (pgvector) extension stores and indexes embeddings but cannot call Azure OpenAI to create them.
e250de0ff1e9.azure_storage: azure_storage imports and exports data with Azure Blob Storage. Calling Azure OpenAI from SQL needs azure_ai.

c1d4a24994ba.The azure_ai extension with an in-databa: azure_ai calls Azure AI services from SQL. It does not provide a vector index for large data sets.
c1d4a24994ba.The pg_hint_plan extension with an HNSW: pg_hint_plan only influences query plans. It does not reduce HNSW memory needs at this scale.
c1d4a24994ba.The pg_trgm extension with a GIN index o: pg_trgm indexes text for trigram similarity and cannot index vector embeddings.

b332cc184c58.LIKE comparisons cannot use any index wi: The issue is the partial index predicate, not LIKE support in general. The planner uses the index only when the query matches its predicate.
b332cc184c58.Partial indexes are supported only for I: pgvector supports partial HNSW indexes. The query simply has to repeat the index predicate.
b332cc184c58.The partial HNSW index must be rebuilt a: HNSW indexes are maintained as rows are inserted. The scan happens because the filter does not match the predicate.

1c83c6795cad.pgvector HNSW indexes support up to 1,53: The pgvector HNSW and IVFFlat limit for the vector type is 2,000 dimensions, not 1,536.
1c83c6795cad.pgvector HNSW indexes require halfvec co: vector columns can be indexed up to 2,000 dimensions. The failure here is that 3,072 exceeds that limit.
1c83c6795cad.pgvector HNSW indexes support up to 4,00: 4,000 dimensions is the limit for halfvec. vector columns are limited to 2,000, so 3,072 fails.

9a0b45c05ffc.Any time from the portal: Modules cannot be added to an existing Azure Managed Redis cache. They are chosen at creation.
9a0b45c05ffc.After geo-replication is enabled: Geo-replication does not unlock module changes. Modules are selected only when the cache is created.
9a0b45c05ffc.Only after scaling up the SKU: Scaling does not let you add modules to an existing cache. You must create a new cache with RediSearch selected.

0bb1928bef6c.AllKeysLRU: RediSearch requires NoEviction so index data is not evicted silently. LRU policies evict keys under memory pressure.
0bb1928bef6c.VolatileLRU: VolatileLRU evicts keys with an expiry under memory pressure, which RediSearch does not allow.
0bb1928bef6c.VolatileTTL: VolatileTTL evicts keys closest to expiring, which can drop index data. RediSearch needs NoEviction.

eeeb45169af7.Lower the similarity threshold for a cac: A lower threshold accepts less similar prompts as hits, which causes more wrong answers, not fewer.
eeeb45169af7.Increase the cache TTL so entries live l: A longer TTL keeps entries around longer and does nothing to stop a wrong entry from matching.
eeeb45169af7.Switch the vector index from HNSW to FLA: FLAT returns the exact nearest entry, which is still the wrong but similar one. The match threshold decides whether it counts as a hit.

39a2cfc8851d.Service Bus partitioning with the order: A partition key places messages together but does not give one-at-a-time ordered processing per order. Sessions provide that.
39a2cfc8851d.Service Bus duplicate detection with the: Duplicate detection would drop later messages for the same order as duplicates. It does not enforce ordering.
39a2cfc8851d.Event Hubs consumer groups with one grou: Consumer groups are independent views of the whole stream, not per-key ordered queues. Service Bus sessions fit this pattern.

dd555339bb25.Duplicate detection based on SessionId w: Duplicate detection tracks MessageId, not SessionId. Many distinct messages share a SessionId.
dd555339bb25.Sessions with the producer ID set as the: Sessions group and order related messages but do not discard duplicates sent on retry.
dd555339bb25.Dead-lettering based on MaxDeliveryCount: MaxDeliveryCount moves messages that fail processing to the dead-letter queue. It does not stop a sender from enqueuing duplicates.

44cb668e51a4.Dead-lettering on filter evaluation exce: This subscription setting handles rule filter errors. Expired messages need dead-lettering on message expiration.
44cb668e51a4.A MaxDeliveryCount higher than the defau: MaxDeliveryCount governs failed delivery attempts, not expiration. It does not move expired messages to the dead-letter queue.
44cb668e51a4.Auto-forwarding to a dead-letter queue: Auto-forwarding moves messages to another entity as they arrive. Expired messages are dead-lettered only with dead-lettering on expiration.

cd58a2861358.5: The default MaxDeliveryCount for queues and subscriptions is 10, not 5.
cd58a2861358.3: The default is 10 delivery attempts before a message is dead-lettered, not 3.
cd58a2861358.100: 100 is not the default. Service Bus dead-letters a message after 10 failed deliveries by default.

c00cfb59a82c.Standard: Standard supports messages up to 256 KB, far below 50 MB.
c00cfb59a82c.Basic: Basic supports messages up to 256 KB and lacks many features. Large messages need Premium.
c00cfb59a82c.Standard with large message support: Large message support is a Premium feature. Standard is capped at 256 KB per message.

11a44c72c7ac.It retries with exponential backoff for: Event Grid does not retry 400 Bad Request responses. It dead-letters at once if configured, otherwise drops the event.
11a44c72c7ac.It retries up to 30 times and then drops: The 30-attempt retry policy does not apply to 400 errors, which are not retried at all.
11a44c72c7ac.It retries once after 10 seconds, then d: There is no single retry for 400 errors. Event Grid skips retries and dead-letters immediately when configured.

b08e1d834505.Event Grid waits up to 60 seconds for th: Event Grid waits 30 seconds, not 60. After that it marks the delivery failed and schedules a retry.
b08e1d834505.Event Grid treats the delivery as failed: A timeout is retried, not dead-lettered at once. Dead-lettering happens only after retries are exhausted.
The response timeout is 30 seconds, and a timeout leads to a retry, not to dropping the event.

2da9c9daf5e4.10 attempts or 1 hour, whichever comes f: The defaults are 30 delivery attempts and a 1,440-minute event time to live, not 10 attempts and 1 hour.
2da9c9daf5e4.30 attempts or 7 days, whichever comes f: The default event time to live is 24 hours (1,440 minutes), not 7 days.
2da9c9daf5e4.18 attempts or 24 hours, whichever comes: The default maximum is 30 delivery attempts, not 18.

32a52e996f50.Yes, undeliverable events go to a built-: Event Grid has no built-in dead-letter queue. Dead-lettering is off until you set a storage blob container.
32a52e996f50.No, you must configure a Service Bus que: The dead-letter destination for Event Grid is a storage blob container, not a Service Bus queue.
32a52e996f50.Yes, but only for system topics, which u: Dead-lettering is off by default for system topics too. You must configure a blob container yourself.

659d51d32418.Azure Event Grid: Event Grid routes discrete events to handlers. It is not built for streaming millions of telemetry events per second with retention.
659d51d32418.Azure Service Bus: Service Bus is for transactional enterprise messaging, not high-throughput telemetry streaming.
659d51d32418.Azure Queue Storage: Queue Storage is a simple message queue without partitions or stream retention, so it does not fit telemetry streaming at this scale.

83ae05eb6bae.Flex Consumption supports only the in-pr: Flex Consumption runs on Linux only and does not support the in-process model.
83ae05eb6bae.Flex Consumption supports .NET only thro: Flex Consumption supports C# natively with the isolated worker model. Custom handlers are not required.
83ae05eb6bae.Flex Consumption requires .NET in-proces: Always ready instances reduce cold starts but do not enable the in-process model, which Flex Consumption does not support.

4f7f996ce070.Enable deployment slots, because Flex Co: Flex Consumption does not support deployment slots at all.
4f7f996ce070.Use slot swap with preview, because Flex: Swap with preview needs deployment slots, which Flex Consumption does not support.
4f7f996ce070.Use zip deploy with WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PAC: Flex Consumption does not use WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE. Zero-downtime releases use its site update strategies.

d0e0ef8ceeaf.Delegation to Microsoft.Web/serverFarms: Microsoft.Web/serverFarms delegation is used by other App Service plans. Flex Consumption needs Microsoft.App/environments.
d0e0ef8ceeaf.Delegation to Microsoft.ContainerInstanc: This delegation is for Azure Container Instances. Flex Consumption subnets must be delegated to Microsoft.App/environments.
d0e0ef8ceeaf.A service endpoint for Microsoft.Web: A service endpoint does not satisfy the integration requirement. The subnet must be delegated to Microsoft.App/environments.

a8d9738022ee.The blob trigger with the LogsAndContain: LogsAndContainerScan is the polling-based source, which Flex Consumption does not support.
a8d9738022ee.The blob trigger with a shorter polling: Polling-based blob triggers are not supported on Flex Consumption at any interval. Use the Event Grid source.
a8d9738022ee.The blob trigger with always ready insta: Always ready instances reduce cold starts but do not make the polling blob trigger work on Flex Consumption.

95c0ff85b543.anonymous: anonymous means no key is required, so any client could call the function.
95c0ff85b543.user: user is not a valid authLevel for an HTTP trigger. The documented values are anonymous, function and admin.
95c0ff85b543.none: none is not a valid authLevel value. To require a function key, set authLevel to function.

3d8caf27d8a0.Durable Functions with the function chai: Function chaining runs activities one after another, not in parallel, so it does not fan out work.
3d8caf27d8a0.Durable Functions with the monitor patte: The monitor pattern polls a condition in a loop. It does not start parallel activities and aggregate results.
3d8caf27d8a0.A Service Bus trigger with batch receivi: Batch receiving processes several messages per call but has no reliable fan-in step to aggregate results.

d7a187482899.Nothing, since purge protection is neede: Soft delete alone keeps deleted secrets for the retention period. Purge protection only blocks early permanent deletion.
d7a187482899.Recreate it with the same name, since so: A soft-deleted secret keeps its name reserved until it is purged or recovered, so you recover it instead.
d7a187482899.Restore it from the vault's automatic da: Key Vault has no automatic daily backup to restore from. Soft delete recovery is the built-in way back.

917cf993960b.Soft delete: Soft delete keeps deleted objects for a retention period, but a user with purge permission can still delete them permanently.
917cf993960b.Resource locks: A resource lock protects the vault resource itself, not the secrets inside it from being purged.
917cf993960b.Azure RBAC authorization: RBAC decides who can act on secrets but an authorized admin could still purge them. Purge protection blocks purging for everyone.

f41550d0ee42.@KeyVault(SecretUri=https://myvault.vaul: The reference prefix must be @Microsoft.KeyVault. This shortened form is not recognized by App Service.
f41550d0ee42.{\"uri\":\"https://myvault.vault.azure.n: This JSON is the value format of an App Configuration Key Vault reference, not an App Service app setting reference.
f41550d0ee42.@Microsoft.AppConfiguration(Endpoint=htt: This syntax references a value in App Configuration, not a secret in Key Vault.

a54dd0d22895.Watch every key individually and refresh: Refreshing key by key can load a half-finished set of changes. A sentinel key lets clients reload everything together.
a54dd0d22895.Set the cache expiration to zero so all: This floods the store with requests and still loads changes as they land, not when the release is ready.
a54dd0d22895.Subscribe to Event Grid and restart the: Reacting to every key change still picks up partial updates. The sentinel key marks when the full set is ready.

47274003d86f.An App Configuration feature flag with a: A time window filter enables a feature between dates. It cannot target a group or a percentage of users.
47274003d86f.An App Configuration key with a label fo: Labels separate versions of a key, such as by environment. They do not target individual users or percentages.
47274003d86f.An App Service slot with 10% traffic rou: Slot traffic routing sends a random 10% of all users, not 10% of a beta group, and requires a separate deployment.

5dcbce8f3bec.requests | summarize percentile(duration: operation_Id identifies a single operation instance, so this groups per request, not per operation name.
5dcbce8f3bec.requests | top 95 by duration | summariz: top 95 returns the 95 slowest rows, not a percentile, and summarize by alone computes no duration value.
5dcbce8f3bec.requests | summarize percentiles(duratio: This returns the 5th percentile, not the 95th.

ff8198b0842c.join on operation_Name: operation_Name is shared by every request to the same route, so it would match unrelated exceptions. operation_Id links one operation.
ff8198b0842c.union with exceptions: union stacks the two tables without matching rows, so failed requests are not linked to their exceptions.
ff8198b0842c.mv-expand operation_Id: mv-expand expands array values into rows. It does not combine two tables.

ba4f0829eccd.summarize count() by bin(timestamp, 1h): A pie chart shows proportions, not a line over time. render timechart draws a time series.
barchart draws horizontal bars, not a line chart over time.
ba4f0829eccd.summarize count() by bin(timestamp, 1d): bin(timestamp, 1d) groups by day, not by hour.

56ff8f81f4a1.The OpenCensus Azure exporter with the i: OpenCensus is retired, and instrumentation keys are being replaced by connection strings. The OpenTelemetry Distro is the current option.
56ff8f81f4a1.The Azure Monitor Agent with a data coll: Azure Monitor Agent collects machine logs and performance data. It does not instrument a Python app for traces and metrics.
56ff8f81f4a1.The Azure Monitor Ingestion client with: The Ingestion client sends custom logs to Log Analytics tables. It does not produce traces and metrics for Application Insights.

af65a954f31f.A daily cap on the Log Analytics workspa: A daily cap stops ingestion once reached, so later telemetry is lost and the data is not representative.
af65a954f31f.Shorter retention on the Log Analytics w: Retention affects how long data is stored, not how much is ingested, so ingestion cost stays the same.
af65a954f31f.Live Metrics disabled in the OpenTelemet: Live Metrics data is streamed and not stored, so turning it off does not cut ingested volume.
